summary: Create Jenkins jobs config script
description:
*What*
Create a Groovy script which will run on Jenkins to create the required jobs
*Why*
The Jenkins management server requires some existing Jenkins jobs to perform the backup restorations. These should be created during the build of the image. 
*How*
Jenkins features in in-built functionality to run Groovy script which can be used to perform various Jenkins management tasks and configurations. Create a script which uses XML job definitions to create the jobs.
creator: rshelly

summary: Create Jenkins SMTP server config script
description:
*What*
Create a Groovy script which will configure the SMTP server on Jenkins.
*Why*
Jenkins requires a configuration of an SMTP server in order to send email notifications of jobs. This configuration should be completed during the build of the image of the rather than by the user.
*How*
Jenkins features in in-built functionality to run Groovy script which can be used to perform various Jenkins management tasks and configurations.
creator: rshelly

summary: Create Jenkins configuration groovy script
description:
*What*
Create a Groovy script which will run on Jenkins to perform the initial setup including admin user creation.
*Why*
As the Jenkins server is abstracted away from the user so too should the initial setup of the Jenkins server which is usually performed at the Jenkins console when first run. Therefore, this should be completed during the image build.
*How*
Jenkins features in in-built functionality to run Groovy script which can be used to perform various Jenkins management tasks and configurations.
creator: rshelly

summary: Create Job definition files
description:
*What*
Create job definition files for each of the default jobs on the Jenkins server.
*Why*
The Jenkins server image will need jobs to be configured during the build which will then be used by the system. Create definition files for these jobs so that they can be created during the Jenkins image build
*How*
Creating the jobs during the build will be done by a Groovy script, which requires the job definitions as XML. Therefore export the XML job configuration files from the exiting jobs on the development Jenkins server. These were created using Jenkins Job builder.

summary: Package the basic Jenkins jobs so they can be automatically created
description:
*What*
Create Jenkins Job Builder yaml files for all the pre-existing Jenkins jobs.
*Why*
The final system will need to be packaged in some way so that new users can quickly start using it with needing to configure it. The system will require some Jenkins jobs to exist before the user starts using it. e.g.
* a job to decrypt backup files
* a job to deploy a server with the relevant DBMS
* a job to import backups into the DBMS on the server
* a pipeline that performs a full single backup restoration
These jobs should not be configured by the user, they are the building blocks that enable a user to run restorations. Therefore there needs to be some automated method of creating and configuring these jobs when the user initially install/deploys the system.
*How*
[Jenkins Job Builder| can be used to define jobs as _yaml_ or _json_ files which can be used to create jobs on a Jenkins server.
creator: rshelly

This pointed out that the terraform commands may create and access files and directories outside of the request's workspace e.g.: /mnt/vagrant/terraform-log772594896 , /root/.terraform.d . While the request workspace was /dd-master/AKIAJZOBIFUZIJ2F43GQ.
Thus, terraform should be completely separated by using the hashicorp/terraform:light container

description:
This epic serves as a catch-all place for prototyping the testing infrastructure we need to have for successful development of our new mobile platform.
These are the assumptions that will guide the POCs:
* the primary delivery process for our services will be [ansible playbook bundles| deployed on openshift through [ansible service broker| which means that PR-testing of apb updates has high priority
* we expect the services to be capable of working stand-alone, which means that bulk of functional integration testing can happen outside of openshift
* we expect the mobile client libraries to be usable outside of the on-device mobile-runtime
* for any service(s)/openshift/mobile-clien(s) integration, there should be an end-to-end setup path, involving just cli/api use, not involving UI
* any js-based UI should have underlying api-library testable outside of browser
* all code should unit tests run on PRs, code-coverage metrics and only rising trend of code covered with PR's
End goal of this epic is to challenge, or validate these assumptions with POC tasks and prepare the tooling, infrastructure and environment for application of the valid assumptions.
creator: adamsaleh

summary: Service Discovery in Prometheus without cluster view
description:
Current understanding of Prometheus inside Openshift requires cluster view permission, I briefly discussed this with the Prometheus team, who pointed out a way to make this work without requiring the cluster permissions:
{quote}10:47:18 pbrookes: Hey Everyone, I have been doing some work on running Prometheus on Openshift, and using the kubernetes_sd_config to pick up new services to poll for metrics. I have got this working but had to give the default user in the prometheus namespace cluster view permissions
10:47:48 pbrookes: I was hoping there might be a solution that would make this work without having to give cluster permissions, even if it was only able to poll services running in the same namespace
10:47:56 brancz: It doesn't need that
10:47:59 pbrookes: is this the right place to discuss that, or can you point me in the right direction?
10:48:24 brancz: Also that's a user question, the #prometheus channel and prometheus-users mailing list would be the appropriate place to dicsuss this.
10:48:42 pbrookes: brancz: ok, thanks, I will head over there!
10:49:19 brancz: Prometheus can be configured to need exactly the permissions you want eg. per namespace, multiple namespaces, or cluster wide if that's how you want to use Prometheus.
10:52:22 pbrookes: brancz: is that a sub-config of the kubernetes_sd_config, or a separate configuration setting? I don't suppose you have a link to it's docs?
10:53:43 brancz: pbrookes: 
10:53:59 brancz: We didn't mention this explicitly, which we should probably fix.
10:54:12 brancz: The last option in the reference is "namespaces"
10:55:02 brancz: If you omit it, it defaults to all namespaces, thus requires a ClusteRole, if you specify a list of namespaces, it will only require Roles in those respective namespaces.
10:55:15 brancz: For further discussion let's rather jump on #prometheus
10:57:40 pbrookes: brancz: that is awesome, thanks{quote}
creator: pbrookes@redhat.com

So we will try it out on kubernetes directly. Locally you can get Kubernetes up and runining using minikube 
- Identify a tutorial and walkthrough the set up to allow us to get a better understanding

summary: [apb] Include redis in the apicast installation
description:
*What*

*Why*
redis is required by apicast to store auth session information.
*How*
Add a redis service & deployment to the apb provision for 3scale/apicast.
To avoid clashing with the fh-sync-server's 'redis', it's best to have a prefix or suffix to the redis resource names e.g. "apicast-redis"
Then, in the APICast deployment, set the default value for the REDIS_URL environment variable to "redis://redis-apicast:6379"
It's important to set REDIS_URL rather than REDIS_HOST and/or REDIS_PORT, as they may conflict with automatically injected env vars if a service called 'redis' already exists in the project (which could be the case if running fh-sync-server)

summary: [ui] modify the 3scale integration for sync to force choosing an auth option
description:
*What*
3scale requires an authentication type. -We have two available (oauth and api keys) (user keys are not being considered for this POC) when enabling 3scale in a service integration screen we want to force users to choose an authentication method.-
-We are going to enable only api key auth in this iteration.- We are defaulting to api key auth.
*Why*
Choosing an auth option will prevent unusual scenarios where 3scale is being used for auth via App ID/Apps, while Keycloak is being used separately for auth via an Authorization header. This would mean the client/app would need to send 2 sets of headers for Auth.
The auth types should be mutually exclusive to avoid confusion, and potential combinatoric explosion of possible scenarios.
*How*
In the sync screen if 3scale is available present an auth drop down that has to be picked before the user can click the create button. The options should be "App ID/App Key" and "Keycloak". Keycloak can be greyed out if it isn't provisioned in the current Project.
The auth type should be configurable afterward, which would allow switching to/from App ID/App Keys and Keycloak (Oauth)
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: Add api key protection to sync
description:
*What*
We want to leverage the API keys we create as a simple authentication mechanism. 
*How*
When a user enables the 'API Keys' integration for fh-sync-server, it should create a secret with any Mobile Apps app id's and api keys in it.
That secret should be mounted into fh-sync-server.
fh-sync-server should look at the app_id & app_key headers with each sync request and ensure they are in this secret.
Whenever a new Mobile App is created, the secret should be updated with the new Apps app_id & api_key so fh-sync-server will accept requests from the new App.

summary: [server] Change sdk config to check for apicast integration
description:
*What*
When a service (fh-sync-server in this case) is protected by apicast, we want to return the route that apicast knows to forward to that service.
The App ID & App Key should also be returned to the client so it can include them in all requests to apicast.
*How*
Check the sync secret to see if the '3scale' integration is enabled.
If it is, look up the 3scale secret to find the apicast rout, app id & app key.
The apicast route should be set as the sync uri in the sync config.
The app id & app key can be added to the sync config.

These operations should be done via the service configure API. As the configure API will create a binding, it should return the apb pod name(s) that are created

summary: [apb] Create bind implementation for interacting with 3scale via API Keys
description:
*What*
We want users to be able to decide which of their services to protect behind apicast and to do this per service. 
*How*
Create an 3scale bind implementation that can call out to the 3scale API to setup an integration for the configured service url (Sync in this case). This bind will need to accept multi parameters that should be sent to it via the MCP for creating the integration. 
* APIcast Route (deployed into the namespace by the 3Scale provision)
* Sync Service Route (deployed already)
* App Key (key value to create in the 3Scale Application to use for protection)
* Secret name where the access token, domain and service ID are stored
* Secret name to update with the App ID & App Key after bind
This bind apb will update the existing 3Scale secret to have the following for SDK configuration (see FH-4232 for how the configuration will get back to the Mobile App).
* APIcast Route (passed into the binding)
* App ID (got during the binding)
* App Key (passed into the binding)
*NOTE: the provision will need to be updated to include a 'service_id' parameter. This is the ID of an existing service in the user's 3Scale account that will be reconfigured for protecting Sync. The reason for re-using an existing service is due to limits of 1 service in the trial a/c and the inability to delete a service.*
*QUESTION: How/When and by Who (UI or MCP) does the Sync secret get updated to say the 3scale integration is 'enabled'?*
API Docs 
See comment below for what the bind steps will actually do against the 3Scale API
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: [UI] Allow Users to generate & show a build artifact download URL in the UI
description:
*What*
Using the server logic in FH-4215, allow the user to generate an artifact download url & present it in the UI.
*Why*
So users can download a build artifact to their device without requiring additional auth steps.
This will facilitate easy install of binaries, and speed up the Users development flow.
*How*
* On the 'Mobile App' > 'Build History' tab, show a button beside each build to 'Generate a Unique Download URL'.
* Include info on what this will do, and how long the URL will be valid for (see FH-4215 for details).
* This button will call to the MCP server to generate a download URL.
* The download URL will then be shown instead of the 'Generate' button.
* There will only be 2 states for this
** Either the 'Generate' button is shown as there is no download URL (or the download URL has expired). 
** Or the Download URL will be shown
* An option to show a QR code version of the Download URL can be shown. This could be a button beside the download URL link e.g. 'Show QR Code'
creator: davmarti@redhat.com

summary: Allow temporary download url to be generated
description:
*What*
To allow someone to send a link to allow build to be downloaded, we want to create a temporary token that will be used as part of an mcp url to allow downloading the binary.
*How*
Add an endpoint to the server for creating build download url. This endpoint will generate a token and attach it as a annotation to to the specified app build. It will also create a timestamp on the build for when the token will become invalid. 
Then it will return an MCP url for downloading the binary with the token appended as a query param.
In a second endpoint, we will check the token and the timestamp on the build. If valid we will use our service account token to proxy through to Jenkins and retrieve the artefact.

summary: Add Support for Authentication using the old Android System Browser
description:
h6. What
On versions of Android less than 4.4, the Android System Browser is the default browser in the Android OS. On versions later then 4.4, Chrome is the default browser. The majrority of the emulator devices do not come with the Play Store installed (and as a result chrome isn't installed either). Only the Nexus 5X and Nexus 5 Devices in Android Studio come with the chrome browser. 
Therefore only hardware devices running API level 19 or lower are affected,
h6. How 
The issue is caused by the System Browser not allowing mixed SSL sessions by default. This is because our Keycloak test instance uses HTTPS in some parts and HTTP elsewhere. The error happens when the redirect to Keycloak lands on a HTTPS page, but the form to submit the user credentials is being POSTed to a HTTP endpoint.
h6. Why
To allow compatibility with Android devices running 4.4 or API level 19 and lower were the user doesn't have another browser installed on the device like chrome or firefox.
creator: tjackman_jira

summary: Look at extending the Jenkins sync plugin to sync secrets
description:
*What*
We need to be able to specify secrets that contain build credentials as part of a build config and have them synced to Jenkins as credentials.
Credentials for doing App Builds (e.g. developer certificates, keys, profiles) can be added to Jenkins as Credentials (similar to done for the 4.x build farm by millicore ). However, with the 5.x build farm integration looking to leverage the OpenShift Jenkins integration (the OpenShift Sync plugin) as much as possible. be adding/updating OpenShift resources and let the OpenShift Sync plugin take care of creating/updating things in Jenkins. There is currently no way to add or reference arbitrary Secrets in a BuildConfig and have Jenkins Credentials created for them. Only source secrets are converted to credentials, 
*How*
Under the definition of a buildconfig we see a list of source secrets can be added. 
The Jenkins sync plugin does not currently make use of these. We would like to add this functionality in order to create the build credentials needed.
The code that currently does something similar is located:
It would probably be a good idea to reach out to the maintainers (OpenShift Fabric8) also

When a new mobile app is created in MCP, there is a new API Key generated. Currently when we provision sync, it is unprotected unless you also provision keycloak. However we could add basic protection here by using the API keys we have created.
*How*
When we provision MCP we also create a secret or configmap "mcp-mobile-keys" then whenever a new app is created, we update that secret with a key value pair mobile-app-id:APIKey. 
We would then allow this as an integration for any configured service that we can edit. Similar to the keycloak integration, we would show an option in the UI to allow the secret to be mounted at a specified location (chosen by the user for custom services, but not for our services). Our services would then check for these keys on startup and reload on config change. The app would then simply check a the x-app-api-key and x-app-id headers against the secret values.
In the longer term, it is likely we will want to allow something like 3 scale to be configured with these values.
If keycloak is provisioned, and enabled for a service, we should probably remove the apikey secret as keycloak is much more secure.
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: spike secret creation for adding external services to an mcp instance
description:
*What*
A Mobile service can be provisioned in to any namespace. Something like keycloak could already exist outside of OSCP. These services are not forced to be in the same namespace as the mcp. However we will still want to provide integrations to these services and represent them in the mcp UI.
*How*
Mobile services are currently represented by the existence of a secret that has the name of the known mobile service in it. To represent an external service we will want to create a secret in the same namespace as the mcp that has the required details for targeting that external service from the mcp and mobile clients. This secret should have a label or annotation to flag it as external. 
A usecase we can work from is:
I do not want to provision a keycloak into every namespace, I want it to be shared across my mobile projects and consumed by several mobile clients.
It is worth noting that in a situation where sync is provisioned in the mcp namespace and keycloak in another we would need to create a public client and bearer only client to allow sync to be protected by the keycloak server
In a situation where sync is provisioned in a different namespace and keycloak in a different namespace and mcp in a third namespace, I don't think we can support protecting the sync server with keycloak. Perhaps adding docs to instruct a developer what they need to do in order to manually mount the config would be an option here.
Another usecase is :
I have a custom app with a rest api and I want to integrate it into my mobile client. In this case the mcp ui would allow them to create a custom service with a name and the location and credentials etc which would then be created as a secret in the namespace.
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: Setup a 'Hybrid' MCP using UI extensions & server per namespace
description:
*What*
The 'hybrid' approach will leverage OpenShift UI extensions for the UI,
and the deployment of an mcp server per namespace.
The UI will need to talk to the mcp server in that namespace for working with 'Mobile Apps' and 'Mobile Enabled Services'.
*Why*
This approach is based on the first & second phases of the POC.
For the first phase
* the UI was 'in' OpenShift via a UI extension
* the server was a 'kubernetes api server'
* it stored 'mobileapp' resources in etcd
* the server was registered with the kubernetes API Aggregator to extend the kubernetes API
For the second phase
* the UI was completely standalone
* the UI used oauth to login to openshift to get a token 
* the server was deployed per namespace
* the server required a serviceaccount token
* mobile apps were represented as a 'configmap'
* services were represented as a 'secret'
The UI in OpenShift via UI extensions was chosen as the better UX as it made Mobile more discoverable i.e. a Mobile tab in the left nav.
The Server per namespace was chosen as it avoids unnecessary admin privileges required to install the server at the 'cluster level'.
*How*
Combine the UI approach from the first phase with the server approach from the second phase.
creator: davmarti@redhat.com

summary: [Spike, clientsdk] Investigate Keycloak Login Screen Related Functionality Compatibility with a Custom Login Screen
description:
h6. What
The Keycloak login interface features a lot more functionality and features than a traditional login screen. For example:
# 2FA
# User Actions Post Auth
# Brute force detection and lockouts
# Audit of login events
# Social logins
# etc
In Keycloak default login screen on the server, a lot of features in Keycloak are bound to this login interface. If we use out our own login screen, we will break the relationship between the login screen and the keycloak backend features.
If we are going to create out own custom login screens, we should investigate if is possible during authentication if we can manually call endpoints on Keycloak to retrieve/report on the following so we can properly handle them in the mobile client login interface:
* *2FA*
* Has the user setup a 2FA token
* Is this credential type currently enabled
 * *User Actions Post Auth*
* Does the user need to update his profile after login?
* Does the user need to configure OTP after login?
* Does the user need to verify his email after login?
* Does the user need to update his password after login?
* *Brute force detection*
* Is brute force detection enabled in Keycloak for this client?
* What are the maximum amount of retries/intervals between retries etc ?
* Is there a temporary or permanent lockout in place?
* Does keycloak have an endpoint that we can report a lockout too?
* *Audit of Login Events*
* Does keycloak have an endpoint where we can submit login events to the server.
These are some quick examples, but there is likely many more..
h6. Why
If we move to use our own custom login screens instead on the mobile clients, it could break compatibility of a number of key features in Keycloak. This would essentially be re-writing the Keycloak auth features on the login screen in the different mobile platforms - Android, iOS, Cordova.
creator: tjackman_jira

summary: Call to OpenShift on startup to get the server metadata
description:
*Why*
The mcp will use OpenShift as an oauth provider.
When the mcp is deployed on OpenShift, it would make for a poor installation/setup if the user had to manually configure the OpenShift URL.
The OpenShift Master host is exposed as an IP address via an env var (KUBERNETES_MASTER_HOST), but this IP address will not work when sending users to it for oauth authorization. The OpenShift public hostname must be used.
*How*
On mcp startup, make a call to the server metadata endpoint [1]. Based on the response:
* set the appropriate config for the server oauth client [2]
* build the config.js response for the /console/config.js endpoint [3]
The mcp startup should fail if:
* there is no response or an error/invalid response
* the scopes_supported, response_types_supported or grant_types_supported don't include the values used in mcp i.e.
** scopes - user:info user:check-access
** response_types - code token
** grant_types - authorization_code
[1] 
[2] 
[3]

summary: Add Custom Redirect URI Handling to the Keycloak JS Adapter
description:
h6. What
Currently the Keycloak JS Adapter only supports redirects/login/logout handlers to use localhost addresses. This is an issue if you want to sign in via Keycloak in a Native Browser. The browser will try to redirect back to a localhost address, rather than the app via anAppIdentifier:// URI scheme.
h6. Why
For OAuth, the embedded user agent in an app should not be used for performing user authentication, this should be performed by the native browser. A side note, this will also enable Single Sign-on across mobile apps which use the same Keycloak realm.
h6. How
An app identifier URL would also need to be defined - you can use this [plugin| to perform this.
This will be used to perform redirects back to com.app.name namespaces, rather than just URL's. The keycloak redirect config will then follow this path.
To complete the Native Redirect back to the application, we will need to create an Intent in the android implementation with a corresponding Broadcast Receiver for handling the temporary token received from the native browser. The same handling will need to be done for iOS.
creator: tjackman_jira

summary: [idea] Investigate using prometheus to provide dashboard information
description:
*What*
Prometheus is a tool for providing metrics. It is opensource. We want to provide a dashboard view of metrics for mobile applications and services. Prometheus can provide us with a fairly lightweight and powerful way of achieving this (prometheus looks to take about 40MB when running more investigation needed here though).
If we standardised on creating powerful metrics for our mobile services using prometheus it can give us a really nice story for monitoring and "observability" on mobile services. 
*How*
There are several things we may want here
1) provision prometheus to the namespace using a configmap for its configuration
2) as new services are provisioned, to the namespace the mcp will update the configuration for prometheus so that is can start collecting metrics
3) add prometheus metrics to the fh-sync service
4) create a service that will expose prometheus metrics for services (such as keycloak) that don't have prometheus metrics (this service would collect information such as number of failed logins etc)
5) look at creating an apb or standard template that will provision prometheus and the metrics service to a namespace.
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: [Spike]: Investigate the use of API.AI to use voice interactions in android app
description:
In the recent [spike on the Google Assistant | and extending it via the actions API, the use of API.AI was observed. API.AI appears to offer the ability to interpret user voice commands, use ML algorithms to train itself to respond to additional voice commands, and trigger actions based on those commands. While extending the Google Assistant via API.AI seems to restrict developers to just adding to the Google Assistant (as opposed to using API.AI in conjunction with their own apps), API.AI would seem to offer the ability to create standalone API.AI bots that respond to voice commands, and leverage NLP & ML to trigger whatever custom business logic we decide (via http endpoints/ webhooks).
This spike will focus on how API.AI can be used to add voice functionality to an android app, and preferrably illustrate this with a very simple proof of concept/ demo.

summary: Research User Interaction Anomaly Detection Approaches for Mobile
description:
I think we should consider doing User Interaction Anomaly detection research. 
This would basically mean that we build up a record of user interactions in the app, so we can see their typical usage flows and build up a trust score. If we begin to see UI actions that are different from the users normal interactions (ie. lots of requests to sensitive areas or otherwise) then it will lower the trust score. If the trust score goes too low, we should block user actions/ask to re-authenticate.
It might be a good idea to research best approaches and discover if there are any existing libraries.

summary: Create new oAuth2 feature based on RedHat SSO
description:
create a new Oauth2 feature based on RedHat SSO and use a mBaaS Service to provide support for the 3.x and 4.x products
Background: 
(from [~supittma@redhat.com] from email discussion July 21st, 2017; option 3 below being the agreed solution)
So historically RHMAP has offered OAuth2 Support using Google as a IdP. In the SDKs this meant that a Google login page was embedded as a WebView. Google has deprecated support for OAuth2 webviews and has started blocking attempts to log in this way.
Their preferred solution now is to open a web browser and return the code to the application. In Android this is done using Intents and IntentFilters and it is rather easy to do (conceptually). I'm sure iOS, Cordova, and Windows have similar methods.
So our options are 1) fix the SDKs for a service it seems like few are using 2) Add more IdPs that allow webviews and don't support Google for the moment 3) create a new Oauth2 feature based on RedHat SSO and use a mBaaS Service to provide support for the 3.x and 4.x products, or 4) do nothing and just tell our customers it is broken and we won't fix it.
None of these options are great, but this is a blocker for the SDK team getting iOS 11 and Android O support out the door until it is answered.

summary: Investigate improper SplashScreenActivity FH initialization

*Why?*
I found that in multiple templates (at least sync-android-app, pushstarter-android-app) there is improper initialization of FH SDK. 
_FH.init()_ is called when splash screen activity is displayed. When you have some other activity displayed and it goes to the background, Android can then kill the process. You can then return to the activity and in this case new app process is created, it jumps to the previously displayed activity and splash screen with initialization is skipped. This causes app to crash - see FH-3773 for more details.
*What to do?*
* investigate all Android native templates and check where it's happenning
* create tasks for fixing the problem

summary: Spike integrating service config with the client SDK for a JDG service.
description:
*Why*
A major a part of MCP is to enabled mobile integrations with the RedHat suite of products. JDG is a relatively simple one useful for spiking but also useful to a mobile developer as a key value store/cache.
*How*
Add the rest details to a config in the defined format.
Investigate the rest api provided by JDG 
Write or reuse a simple js client for interacting with the REST api.
Create simple app that uses this client
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: Integrate the service config for Sync with the client SDKs
description:
*Why*
We want to understand how we will integrate the different service configurations (based on the binding secrets) into the SDKs. In particular for this spike the Javascript Sync Client, and Keycloak Client.
*How*
We should determine the format of the service config. 
We can create a file with values that point to a running sync service
Build a test app that exercises:
* the sync api via fh-sync-js client
* and a login page via the keycloak client
This SDKs should be configured from the generated service config in the MCP
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: Generate the Client SDK config for Sync, showing it in the MCP UI
description:
*Why*
This will show us how to handle configuration of the SDK.
*How*
* Read a binding secret (for Sync) created by the service catalog after a binding has been created to the service
* Generate the SDK config file, based on the secret
* Show it to the user in the ui with an option to download it
* The downloaded config should be useable with the relevant client SDK
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: Create an APB for provisioning Keycloak and integrate with the OpenShift Mall
description:
*Why*
APB (Ansible Playbook Bundles) are how the Mall via the service catalog and ansible service broker will provision and manage services on OSCP. 
Futher detail:
*How*
Setup the Mall 
Write the APB
Understand how to get the APB into the service catalog via service broker
Reach out to the Openshift team and the ansiblile service broker team (#asbroker) on irc
*Outcome*
Be able to provision the Keycloak service via the catalog/mall.
create a realm for the same namespace (with unique name).
create a secret in the same namespace as the keycloak instance that has the admin credentials
This APB is not meant to be an official APB for installing Keycloak. This is to enable a POC.
Keycloak terminology:
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: Create a POC sync service to be deployed on OSCP
description:
*Why*
Sync is an important mobile service that will be a key offering for mobile on OSCP. So we will need to be able to deploy it to OSCP which is not currently possible.
*How*
Using a basic express app, setup the sync module as a set of routes
Create OpenShift templates using our MBaaS node components as an example.
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

summary: Spike MCP authenticating via RHSSO using OSCP as Oauth Provider
description:
*Why*
We want a unified and standard way of doing authentication. RHSSO is the chosen product to integrate with.
We should also look to use a standard authentication and authorisation method. OSCP supports oauth2 and we want to investigate using OSCP as an oauth provider via RHSSO as we will need to heavily interact with the OSCP API from MCP.
*How*
Deploy an RHSSO in OSCP
Configure it to use OSCP as an oauth2 provider
Investigate if there is an RHSSO js client that we can use.
We should reach out to the RHSSO team for more information.
Prove some kind of interaction with OSCP (IE listing resources such as Services)
We may be able to achieve this without the actual MCP web client spike as it can be done as a standalone investigation.
creator: cbrookes@redhat.com

*How*

Using the Openshift web commons library :
*Concerns*
Authentication: If needed, we should use a hard coded authentication token as figuring out how auth works is part of another spike.

summary: optimise sync mongodb data pruning
description:
h3. Why
The sync framework need to prune the following data it's creating:
* queue messages
* datasetClients and records data
At the moment, the approach to implement this is to have a function runs every x minutes and remove the data.
This does cause some problems:
* extra configurations that developers need to understand
* when there are multiple workers running, it's possible to cause race conditions
h3. What
To address these problems, we can:
* consider using mongodb TTL to remove old data. This is especially useful for queue messages
* try make sure only 1 worker will remove the dataset clients and it's records.

summary: Allow concurrent tasks to be taken from the queue by a single worker
description:
*What*
Allow concurrent tasks to be taken from the queue by a single worker
*Why*
To allow a developer to make better use of the CPU(s) in the event of slow asynchronous tasks.
For example, a dataset backend is quite slow (5 seconds per request), and there is only 1 cloud app running with no clustering or multiple pods.
This would mean there is at least 5 seconds between each item being taken off the queue and being processed. While an item is being processed, the CPU is relatively idle as it is waiting for the dataset backend to respond.
The single worker processes items on the queue synchronously.
Currently, the only way to have multiple items on the queue being processed at the same time is to scale up to multiple workers via cluster forking or by running multiple Pods. However, that would be inefficient in this example as the CPU is being underutilised.
It would be more efficient to process multiple items on the queue at the same time in that 1 worker as there is enough CPU cycles available to do that.
*Suggestions*
* add a worker concurrency flag, with a default value of 1
* add tests for changing the flag and verify it behaves as expected
creator: davmarti@redhat.com

summary: investigate if it's possible to run another app to process the data generated by the existing app
description:
h3. Why
This is a request from the customer (Simense). The idea is that the existing app will be responsible for accepting requests and put the data in the database. Another app will be created to process the data from the database as quickly as possible. 
There are a few benefits if we can support this:
1. another options to scale the sync server even further
2. allow developer to separate HTTP requests handling vs. sync processing. Changes to any one of them will not affect the other.
h3. What
Investigate if this is possible. Based on the current design, it should be. We need to:
* allow developers to override the mongodb url and redis url via env var

summary: introduce backoff strategies for workers to reduce the resource usage of the sync server
description:
h3. Why
While doing the load testing, I noticed that if the worker interval is set to a relative low value, it will increase the load on the sync server, even when there is nothing to process in the queue.
Given that the app will do other things as well, the sync server should not consume that much resource when there is no jobs to run. We should slow down the worker interval when there is no jobs to process, and then set it to the normal rate once the jobs are created.
h3. What
we should introduce a backoff strategies for workers. This will kick in once there are no jobs to process. It will be reset once there are jobs created again.
Developers should be able to override the configuration for each worker.

summary: add caching for dataset client records to improve performance of the syncRecords API
description:
h3. Why
While running the load tests against the `syncAll` endpoint that is calling both `sync` and `syncRecords` API, we see a big drop in terms of performance. From the metrics, we can see most of the time is spent on read the dataset client and its records. Given that this data is only changing when the sync loop runs, we can add caching to improve the performance.
h3. What
1. introduce a configuration option to enable/disable the cache.
2. When enabled, cache the results from `doReadDatasetClientWithRecords` using redis. Invalidate the cache everytime when `doUpdateDatasetClientWithRecords` is called. Read the results from cache if possible.

summary: Write a guide for configuring Sync processor intervals based on available stats
description:
*What*
Write a guide for configuring Sync processor intervals based on available stats
*Why*
So developers can tweak it to best manage the expected load of their app.
*How*
How to best manage the load depends on the developer too. For example, should it:
* continue to respond to client calls as quick as possible (high processor interval)
* prioritise pending updates (low pending processor interval)
The effect of changing the processor interval for each processor (sync, pending, ack) should be tested and understood as part of writing this guide.
Probably involves running some tests (e.g. `ab` or `vegeta` to get feedback on the behaviour).

summary: Setup a minimal sync-based cloud app + client
description:
h3. Why
From RAINCATCH-618 we've identified a potential memory leak caused by idle connected sync clients (see attached screenshot, client connects at ~7:55). In order to investigate it further, we need a minimal sync-based app to replicate this.
h3. How
Create a bare-bones cloud app and companion client app that will connect and sync at {{sync_interval}} times. A single dataset is enough and no data changes from the client are needed.
The cloud app should use fh-component-metrics to report to a grafana installation.
If possible a cli-based client would be ideal, instead of having to keep a browser running a web client app (phantomjs could be an acceptable alternative).
The actual long-running tests and result analysis are outside of the scope of this issue, and should be done in a follow-up issue.

creator: davmarti@redhat.com

summary: Dataset Clients should not be removed to avoid problems with deferred updates for inactive clients
description:
*What*
Make changes to the code so that inactive dataset clients will not be removed immediately from the db
*Why*
At the moment, when a dataset client is being inactive (no client has accessed it for a period time), the dataset client will be removed & the records of the dataset client will be checked and cleaned up. However, this has caused a few issues:
1. if there are some deferred sync requests, there is a chance the dataset client is being deleted completed by the time the sync request is being processed (Related to 
2. the delete dataset client operation is an expensive operation. If the inactive period is set too low, it could have an impact on the performance of the system.
3. If the dataset client back later on, the whole datasetclient & dataset client records have to be recreated again.
Based on those issues, it's better not to delete the dataset client when a dataset client become inactive.
*How*
* We will leave them in the database but will not sync them with the backend, until the next sync request is invoked for those dataset clients.
* we will also create a repeat job that will check the dataset clients periodically, and delete them based on a configuration that can be set by the developer.
creator: davmarti@redhat.com

summary: Change fh-mbaas-api to return Error objects to callbacks in all exceptional cases
description:
While working on FH-3220 to review the logging in the sync framework, I noticed that when passing errors to callbacks, we lack consistency: sometimes we pass an {{Error}} object, sometimes we pass a {{String}} instead, and in other cases it's not easy to determine what the type of the potential first parameter to the callback is by looking at the code.
It would seem to make sense to change this so that we always use {{Error}} objects for this purpose. This way, users (and us!) will know what to expect in their calling code. If we're currently passing any {{String}} or other types as errors to external callers, then changing this should probably be considered a breaking change, worthy of a semver major version bump.
In addition to just changing to {{Error}} objects, we should consider using the [VError| module from Joyent, to wrap Errors with additional context as we pass them around internally, before eventually giving them to an external caller. Again, I think this would be beneficial to both external callers and ourselves internally.
creator: gryan@redhat.com

summary: Investigate how to do realtime sync via websockets
description:
*What*
Investigate how to do realtime sync via websockets
*Why*
Both the current sync framework (fh-mbaas-api <=6), and the sync framework changes to support horizontal scalability are 'eventual sync' implementations.
This means any changes applied on the client will eventually be applied to the dataset backend. These changes will also eventually be propagated to any other active clients.
A recommendation from [~jfrizell@redhat.com] is to figure out the touchpoints for integrating websockets, with the intention of moving to realtime sync, as it may be a valueable feature of sync.
*Suggestions*
* Identify any sync APIs that may have to change
* Identify any config that is based on their being a sync loop (e.g. sync_frequency, crash retry count)
* Identify how much of the client & server code would be replaced by the websockets layer
* How to maintain backwards compatibility for Environments that don't support websockets
* How to notify multiple clients of updates as they are processed
Based on the report produced by this issue, there may be a followup Epic, or PRD.
creator: davmarti@redhat.com

summary: Change the sync logger to allow passing in a logger implementation
description:
*What*
Change the sync logger to allow passing in a logger implementation
*Why*
The current logger in the sync framework [1] is a wrapper around winston.
There are 2 problems with this approach:
* there is no way for a different logger used by a developer to be re-used by the sync framework, meaning potentially 2 different formats of logging in the app logs
* the logging wrapper only has a single logging function, doLog, rather than following a standard interface e.g. logger.error, logger.warn, logger.info. The way to do different log levels is to pass in a string as the 2nd parameter e.g. 'error'
*Suggestions*
* figure out what the most popular logger is in node.js (console.log?), and seeing how logging in modules is usually handled
* support the interface of this logger, meaning most developers can pass in an instance of that logger
* suggest in the docs to wrap any other loggers to conform to that interface before passing in (or let a default logger of our choice do logging)
[1]

summary: Add a cleanup task for each of the sync queues in mongodb
description:
*What*
Add a cleanup task for each of the sync queues in mongodb
*Why*
The mongodb-queue module [1] keeps all queued jobs in mongodb, even after they have been 'taken' from the queue and processed.
Once processed and acked, they are marked as 'deleted'.
There is a 'cleanup' function that will remove any deleted jobs [2], but this must be manually invoked.
*Suggestions*
* -call cleanup after each ack of a job-
* -add a node-cron job that periodically calls cleanup for each queue-
* -if we want to keep all jobs as an audit log for a particular period of time, we could use node-cron to send a delete query to mongodb for jobs that are deleted & older than a certain time (e.g. 1 day). This approach would need to know about the inner workings of the mongodb-queue module and the collection(s) it uses-
* add config values for the time to keep complete jobs in the queue (as an audit log). On startup, run a query for each queue to remove any old jobs, and set an interval for it to be run again at a regular interval.
[1] 
[2]

summary: Assert the behaviour of scaling the current sync server
description:
Taken from sync doc:
{code}
If the current sync server code were horizontally scaled (e.g. via node.js cluster workers), the following would happen:
Depending on the number of active Clients and number of Cluster Workers, there may be unnecessary syncs happening for datasets. For example, if 3 Clients make a call to a different worker (load balanced) at 0, 1 and 2 seconds, those workers will mark the DataSet Client for sync at 10, 11 & 12 seconds respectively. This could cause unwanted load on the DataSet Backend as it does 3 syncs (doLists) in quick succession even though the sync frequency should only be 10 seconds.
After the above scenario, there may also be inconsistency on the Clients depending on which worker their next request gets through to. For example, if there was an new record added between the 10 & 11 second sync, those 2 workers will have a different dataset hash. Depending on which worker each Client gets load balanced to next, they may get the correct latest data, or may be told to delete the record that the worker think exists.
{code}
We should use this behaviour to create a test that would currently fail, where the sync server is clustered with two workers. The idea is that once the horizontal scaling work has been completed, this test should pass.

summary: Assert that getUID will retrieve the new UID of a record after a successful creation
description:

The getUID function in the client API is supposed to map between these. For example, providing the hash of the created record should do one of two things:
* If the record has not been persisted on the server, return the hash of the record as that is still it's UID.
* If the record has been persisted on the server, return the MongoDB UID of the record as that is now the records actual UID.
creator: akeating-1

summary: implement the sync records http handler

h3. Why

** If there is, use that to compare with the records, and after getting the delta, iterate through all those records, and if any of them is in the applied_but_not_in_cache collection, or if in the pending queue, remove them from the delta. This way the client will keep its value. See for sample gist
** The global hash should be from the last sync loop
** If there is no cache, just respond empty object. The sync loop will run at some point in the future to populate the cache.
*** This situation would be very rare as a syncRecords should only be triggered on the client if a sync loop happened on the cloud and a there is a different global hash from the client. Therefore this situation should only happen if something happens redis (flush?) between the sync loop and the syncRecords call from the client.

summary: Allow the client sync frequency to be set by the server
description:
Currently an issue pops up regularly around users believing that setting the sync frequency on the client would also set the sync frequency of the dataset on the server. This is not the case and can cause two sync loops on the server each sync frequency if the client frequency is less than the server frequency.
If we were to allow the sync frequency for a dataset that is set on the server to be passed down to the client, we might be able to remove the misunderstanding by not needing users to set the sync frequency on both.
Setting the sync frequency for a dataset on the client would take precedence over the server sync frequency, allowing clients to decide to sync less often if they choose to.

summary: Implement a queue factory to create mongodb-backed queues
description:
h3. Why
In order to scale the sync server, we need to allow sync requests to be processed by multiple processes. The best way to do it is to use queues. We also need persisted queues and HA to make sure the data won't be lost if the process crashes. Based on those requirements, we need to implement a queue backed up by mongodb. (We don't have HA for redis at the moment)
h3. What
Implement a queue factory can create queues based on a given name. Each of the queue should have the following interfaces (minimum):
* addJob - add a new job to the queue
* process - register a worker to get the oldest job off the queue and process it
The queue should be backed up by mongodb.
h3. Other considerations
For testing purpose, we should have a queue implementation that is in-memory.
creator: weil@redhat.com

This will mean the data is never persisted.
We should have a test for this functionality, using a mock sync server.
creator: akeating-1

summary: Update the sync client to mark pending inFlight records as crashed after X number of sync loops
description:
*What*
Update the sync client to mark pending inFlight records as crashed after X number of sync loops
*Why*
This client change is to support a backend change where the server will respond early after accepting pending records, rather than accepting *and* processing pending records then responding.
In this scenario it is possible for the cloud app to crash after accepting the pending records and responding, but before the pending records are processed. Therefore, it is currently possible in the client for pending inFlight records to be stuck in that state indefinitely.
The only way currently to get those records to be resent is to mark them as crashed, which would happen if the error callback is called for a sync call
 For example, if the cloud app goes offline, all pending records on the client, including already inFlight records, will be marked as crashed.
*How*
Suggesting adding a new config for the number of sync loops to wait before marking an inFlight change as crashed.
This check should happen with every successful sync loop e.g. if the config value is 10, only mark pending inFlight records as crashed if they've been inFlight for 10 *successful* sync loops.
creator: davmarti@redhat.com

summary: When server crashes for one sync loop after immediate response the client should mark as crashed and retry

It could also go into `guides/server-side-developer-guide/sync_service.js` in the documentation.
h3. Todo
The issue itself was that a client application had a syncFrequency of 120 seconds, due to this it was expected that the list function on the cloud would only be called every 120 seconds.
However, the cloud has its own syncFrequency which defaults to 10 seconds, this resulted in the list function being called twice every 120 seconds, increasing server load.
By updating the syncFrequency of a dataset on the cloud to match the syncFrequency of the dataset on the client this duplication is removed.

description:
*Story*
As an user with SOAP-based APIs, I want API mapper to be able to parse a provided WSDL and present that API inside the mapper so that I can make some/all of it it available as a mapped JSON API in the platform.
*What*
Add WSDL parsing support to API Mapper.
This includes full WSDL parsing and UI-based interaction. These would need a more complex UI for the mapping and transformation.
*Suggestions*
"Create request from WSDL" wizard.
* Step 1, import WSDL file (url or file upload)
* Step 2, select function to implement 
* Step 3, inform the user of the body params they need to supply in JSON format (since we can't map request bodies or URL params yet)
* Step 4, finished. A new request is created with the appropriate settings already populated to access this API. The user can interact, get a JSON response back (no more soap), and then map it to their hearts content
from [~wtrocki@redhat.com]
{quote}
Done small investigation for this requirement and it feels that's something we cannot do in API mapper with complete rewrite. API MAPPER and generally Express.js is orientated around REST webservices where each endpoint represents resources. WSDL is typically one url that returns large xml with api definition. There are tools to deal with WSDL for node.js that would do way better job than even refactored API mapper. 
Good example here may be . It would generate definition for SOAP based API. 
Suggestion - use and then provide extension for that library to connect it with existing API mapper without any direct changes in API mapper itself.
{quote}
creator: davmarti@redhat.com

summary: Everything should be case sensitive

summary: Add Forms Data Source support to API Mapper

summary: Investigate how to make API Mapper easier to stand-up
description:
*Story*
As a less technical user, I want to be able to easily create an instance of the API Mapper so that I can start using it immediately with no awkward setup steps.
*What*
Investigate how to make API Mapper easier to stand-up
*Why*
So less technical users can make use of the API Mapper
*Suggestions*
API Mapper currently requires a user to do the following to make use of it:
* Make the newly created service public 
* Visit the data browser, and upgrade the database so this application has it's own database. 
* Re-deploy the service
Understand the reasons for each of these steps, and identify ways of simplying them or removing them completely.
For example, if possible, we should deploy the Service with database by default and permissions set to Public.

summary: POC for exporting a cloud app template from an MBaaS and running it on a local MBaaS
description:
*What*
Do an end to end POC for exporting an OSCP3 cloud app template (all its resources) from a remote MBaaS and run it on a local MBaaS
*Why*
The main reason for this is to figure out all the touch points & pain points of doing local cloud app development with a local MBaaS.
The intention is for this to build on the open sourcing of the MBaaS i.e. the developer can run the open source MBaaS locally.
Doing local development to date did not include a running MBaaS. This approach should allow a local dev environment that is more similar to how the cloud app will run in production.
*Suggestions*
- create a cloud app in an RHMAP cluster (both Core & MBaaS), and deploy it to the MBaaS
- manually do an `oc export` of all cloud app resources from the MBaaS
- run the open source MBaaS locally (i.e. completely separate from the cluster where the cloud app was created)
- import the exported cloud app resources to the local MBaaS
- make notes of any changes to config, envvars or code required to get the cloud app working
There may be follow up issues needed to progress this further to a point where it is possible for a developer to do local development relatively easily.
That said, this issue may have a first pass at doing local dev that can be shared in the form of a blog post

summary: Investigate how a service can get Mongo credentials from other cloud app in the same project
description:
*What*
Identify what is the best way for a service to access the database from other cloud apps in the same project. A service should receive the name of the database, port and the needed credentials.
*Why*
When provisioning a Mongo Express as a service into the platform it only has access to the service database. To make Mongo Express useful as a service in RHMAP we would need it to access the cloud app's database so all the DB management tasks for the app could be handled through Mongo Express.
*Workaround*
At the moment we managed to hardcode the cloud app's credentials as env vars for Mongo Express service. This works but it's a slow and error prone process so it would be much better to get that data with no manual intervention.

description:
*What*

*Why*

Having such a template could provide a useful starting point & a reference point for developers who want to focus on minimal resource usage in their Cloud App.

- possibly remove the usage of 
- any other 'default' modules that tend to be used in cloud app templates are up for grabs to leave out of this template. Ideally, the only dependency is the limited $fh API.
Note: This template should probably be added to the platform templates in

summary: CocoaPods 0.37.0 and mix ObjC/Swift framework
description:
Atm fh-ios-swift resuses Objc Sync code. 
However when the Sync code is calling http request, we use the Swift http layer.
For ObjC code to be able to call Swift code in a same framework target we use FeedHenry-Swift.h. In source folder, the content of this file is empty but at runtime it is automatically generated by Xcode.
The framework build fine. Unit tests runs.
However when we try to use fh-ios-swift-sdk in an template app the FeedHenry-Swift.h file fetched by CocoaPods is an empty file. therefore the project won't compile complaining when Sync code is calling Swift code.
As a workaround, in fh-ios-sdk I've added a build phase to copy the content of this file in the source folder. It works ok on local build.
To be tested on Build farm.
creator: corinnekrych_jira

summary: FHSyncClient with NSTimer in background mode
description: FHSyncClient uses the NSTimer class to schedule server sync checks. iOS will kill this timer when app is backgrounded. Therefore, FHSyncClient cannot be used to reliably pull updates down from a server. As of iOS 7, the background mode "background fetch" is recommended for pulling such data. Apple recommends using NSURLSession when making network calls in a background fetch.
